chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Abban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah will send three hundred and thirteen men to a mosque in Mecca. The people of Mecca will know that they were not born from their fathers or grandfathers. Swords will be upon them, written on which are one thousand words; each word is a key to one thousand words. And Allah will send the wind from every valley saying: 'This is the Mahdi; he rules with the ruling of David,' and he does not require any evidence.

key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: The Guided One, referring to the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.بَيِّنَةً: Evidence or proof, indicating the Mahdi's rule is self-evident or divinely sanctioned
key_terms.دَاوُدَ: Prophet David, known for his just rule

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and characteristics of the Mahdi's arrival according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the Mahdi’s emergence with 313 companions to Mecca, emphasizing their miraculous, non-genealogical origin and the divine wind that validates his authority. The comparison to Prophet David’s judgment signifies a rule based on divine wisdom and justice rather than mere political force, reflecting the Shia eschatological expectation of a just global order.
